findings.title: Remove private loader indices from the public model contract
findings.reason: SCENE.main_object/collision_object must equal objects_3d_scene_database[scene].index/collision_object_index. Those are legacy objects_3d_data numbering, not public scene IDs; independent/DCS model providers cannot choose their own model storage without replicating the private EECH loader layout. This is enforced even when all physical values are host-authored.
findings.correction: Correlate via public scene/schema identity and host-authored collider presence. Keep any raw-index comparison inside reference adapter/diagnostics, not campaign public acceptance. Update C/Rust/Lua fields and independent-provider controls accordingly.

findings.title: Read physical NUMBER values before mlua integer coercion
findings.reason: model_f32 receives LuaValue after table.get. Patched Lua5.1 lua_isinteger treats doubles within EPSILON of an integer as Integer, so tiny nonzero/subnormal values reach this function as Integer0 and negative-zero sign is lost. nearest_f32 cannot reconstruct the discarded bits. Existing exact_numbers in the same module explicitly avoids this seam. Explicit hex strings are not affected. Current tests cross already-created Rust f32 values, not this new Lua numeric path.
findings.correction: Use exact raw-Lua numeric extraction with strict number typing, one stateful getter read, retained hex support, signedzero/subnormal/inexact-double fidelity and documented deterministic nearest-single rounding. Add real public callback-crossing tests under engine round-toward-zero and caller-state checks; do not change physical kernel/oracles.

findings.title: Reject a triangle contradicting the installed absence
findings.reason: FOUND checks finite points but never checks host_collision_object[scene]==-1, whereas END and ABSENT are checked against the installed catalogue. A provider can declare an absent model (e.g. scene1241) and return FOUND; C then writes the caller buffer and returnsTRUE despite its own absence declaration.
findings.correction: After replacing raw indices with public host-authored presence, reject FOUND for absent scenes before writing any caller word. Add an actual C/public callback contradiction control alongside END/ABSENT guards.

findings.title: Bound malformed float text and enforce the exact indexed list
findings.reason: Comma text is collected into an unbounded Vec before6/9 length checking. Table parsing stops at the first nil and only reads throughN+1: valid1..N plus an extra value atN+2 is silently accepted, contrary to the documented exactN list. A malformed host answer can force needless allocation or hide an overlong/sparse indexed shape.
findings.correction: Bound text/token parsing atN+1 and validate the intended exact dense indexed shape, preserving single-read getter semantics. Add real Lua extra-after-hole/overlong text controls; valid exact lists and strings must remain accepted.

findings.title: Make requested authority probes finite and fail closed
findings.reason: Durations/frame_ms/sweeps/seed/probe lists are not strictly checked before output and boot. frame_ms=0 yields an infinite numeric-for bound when seconds>0 while frame(0) need not advance. Invalid list items can disappear through nil insertion. Separately a requested model_host_probe refusal is only emitted as ok=false: reference mode can finish healthy after all requested probes fail.
findings.correction: Validate finite bounded scheduling, integral positive frame_ms and bounded integral seed/sweep/scene/depth lists before output/prepare/boot; enforce finite frame/progress bounds. Propagate requested probe failures/missing results to failure/nonzero exit; add real-driver invalid/no-progress/refused-probe controls.

findings.title: Emit strict JSON and check every output operation
findings.reason: Lua5.1 string.format(%q) is Lua quoting, not JSON escaping. A healthy C probe report contains embedded newlines; quoted output can therefore be invalid JSON, and error control bytes have the same problem. write/flush/close results are ignored, allowing truncated/lost evidence with successful exit. Both new emitters use this pattern.
findings.correction: Use a strict control-byte JSON encoder and checked write/flush/close paths, preserving native output bytes rather than normalizing them. Exercise multiline probe text,0..31/quote/backslash/UTF8 errors and output-failure controls through the real scripts.

findings.title: Describe the actual callback retention and user lifetime
findings.reason: Install-once/first-entry wording implies later callbacks are ignored, but set_host overwrites current_host on every non-NULL callback, retaining its user pointer when later entries areNULL. Current Rust production is safe because model_callback ignores user and MODEL owns the provider for the process; the header should not imply an enforced C first-install guarantee.
findings.correction: Either enforce the stated first-install contract or document the actual refresh/retention behavior and callback-user lifetime requirement, distinguishing fixed Rust TLS provider from per-entry HostContext.

findings.title: Distinguish reference answers from altered answers
findings.reason: counted increments found/ended/absent from the reference answer before vanish/inflate/bad_* wrappers replace that answer. Those fields therefore do not count the final altered model replies accepted by C, despite the what-the-provider-answered comment. Native fixture counters can supply the actual accepted counts.
findings.correction: Name/document these as reference-answer counters or count final replies separately. Keep native accepted counters and consequences distinct; do not infer authority from reference counts alone.
